sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: warning versus braking systems, back-up warning versus reverse braking, lane departure warning versus lane keeping assist, and continuation facts on cameras, detection, road-test scoring, parking assist and automation levels
Confusable pairs among driver assistance features, followed by continuation facts that did not fit part C; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A01
Warning technologies exist mainly to alert the driver in specific situations, whether a crash is near or a part of the vehicle is malfunctioning. [A01]
Why it matters: group warning systems; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A02
Depending on the vehicle, the rear camera picture may show up in the rearview mirror, the sun visor, the center console screen or another spot. [A02]
Why it matters: group cameras; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A02
Some newer vehicles use sideview cameras instead of traditional side mirrors. [A02]
Why it matters: group cameras; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A02
In most surround-view systems one camera sits in the middle of the front bumper and two more look down from the side mirrors, and some add audio warnings when you get too close to an obstacle. [A02]
Why it matters: group cameras; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A02
Some detection systems only notice cyclists, pedestrians or obstacles directly in front of the vehicle and moving the same way, so read the owner's manual to learn how your car warns you. [A02]
Why it matters: group detection; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A03
A forward collision warning only warns and leaves the braking to you, whereas automatic emergency braking applies the brakes itself if you fail to respond. [A03]
Why it matters: group safety systems; confusable warning versus automatic braking.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A03
A rear cross-traffic alert only warns that a vehicle is about to cross your backing path, whereas automatic reverse braking applies the brakes itself when you fail to react to a detected obstacle. [A03]
Why it matters: group backing systems; confusable cross-traffic alert versus reverse braking.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A03
A high speed alert sounds when you are speeding, helping you hold a safe speed. [A03]
Why it matters: group warning systems; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A03
Assistance technology can react faster than a person when a vehicle or object suddenly appears ahead, and if that happens during a practical driving test, the examiner decides at their discretion how it is scored. [A03]
Why it matters: group road test; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A03
Safety-critical technologies are those that may prevent a crash or reduce how severe it is. [A03]
Why it matters: group safety systems; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R11 | anchor: A03
A lane departure warning leaves the steering to you: its alerts exist to prompt the driver to steer back toward the middle of the lane after an accidental drift. [A03]
Why it matters: group lane systems; confusable lane departure warning versus lane keeping assist.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R12 | anchor: A04
To use adaptive cruise control, reach your desired speed, switch it on and choose a short, medium or long following gap; advanced versions can slow, stop and restart in traffic jams. [A04]
Why it matters: group convenience; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec07-R13 | anchor: A04
Automatic parallel parking searches for a usable space and guides you into it with prompts such as pulling ahead, shifting to reverse and letting go of the wheel, but you remain responsible for braking and watching around you. [A04]
Why it matters: group convenience; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec07-R14 | anchor: A05
The Society of Automotive Engineers classifies driving automation in levels from zero to five, starting with vehicles that lack the technology and ending with self-driving vehicles. [A05]
Why it matters: group automation levels; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0055]
